followup.note_on_original_markers: SIRSCriteria2OrMore and InfectionSuspected are ~99% in both groups; they have no discriminating power and are not used here.
followup.verdict: Tested, not asserted. (1) On the variables that actually vary, no difference exceeds 10pp (largest: SIRSCritTemperature -9.6pp; flags: none); age differs by at most 8.4pp per band, with Group A carrying more missing age. So no strong patient-mix difference is detected on recorded varying markers - but absence of a >10pp flag is weak evidence, and the earlier shock gap (Hypotensie -4.6pp) plus lower fever in Group A (SIRSCritTemperature -9.6pp) remain directional. (2) No process confound: antibiotics are administered by the same org:group in both A and B (~93-95% group 'A'). (3) Exposure is SUBSTANTIAL, not small: the 83-case pool supplies 40.1% of all simulated cases and 64.8% of affected draws - so pool representativeness genuinely matters and cannot be dismissed. (4) The concern was therefore tested operationally: excluding the 83 pathway entirely moves predicted C1 compliance by only 1.8pp (80.371% -> 78.53%). Case complexity/acuity beyond recorded flags is unobserved, so a fully clean bias test is impossible from this log. The binding defence does not rest on pool representativeness: every candidate antibiotics time is CAPPED AT THE BASELINE (delay only removed, never added), bounding optimism independently of pool composition.
